# geniro's MCP tools

Every tool geniro's own MCP endpoint serves (`call_agent`, `show_chart`, `propose_plan`, …) lives in `apps/daemon/src/v1/mcp/tools/<tool-name>/`, in the same shape, extending the shared base class. This applies to editing a tool as much as adding one. (A CLI's slash-command skills, `SkillsService`, are not covered.)

## One tool's directory

`tools/<tool-name>/`, kebab-cased from the wire name (`show_chart` → `show-chart/`), holds exactly:

- `<tool>.tool.ts` — the class: `name`, when it is offered, what a call does. No prose, no schema.
- `<tool>.instructions.ts` — `export function <tool>Instructions(…): string`, the description a model reads.
- `<tool>.schema.ts` — `export function <tool>Schema(…): Record<string, unknown>`, the input schema with field descriptions (a function, so each listing gets a fresh object).
- `<tool>.reader.ts` — reads the model's arguments defensively (never throws; every tool's zod argument reader is `tools/tool-args.ts`) and words the result; spec beside it as `<tool>.reader.spec.ts`.

Instructions and schemas are `.ts`, never `.md` or `.json` — swc copies nothing else into `dist/`, so they would silently be missing from a packaged daemon. Values the text needs are function parameters or imports, never load-time placeholders.

## Base classes

- `McpTool` (`mcp.types.ts`) is the contract: `handles`, `list`, `call`.
- Extend `BaseMcpTool` (`tools/base-mcp-tool.ts`): fill `isOffered`, `instructions`, `inputSchema`, `run`; answer through `this.text(…)` / `this.invalidArgs(…)`. Never override `list` or `call`.
- `CallMcpTool` is the base for agent-to-agent call-runtime tools (offered only to nodes with callees, answers via `envelope(…)`, waits via `waiting(…)`).
- `HistoryMcpTool` is the base for chat-history tools. They are never auto-approved and carry no `readOnlyHint` (codex skips approval for read-only tools). One recorded exception: `read_analyzed_thread` (on `BaseMcpTool`, reusing the history preface) is auto-approved (`agents/utils/host-analysis.ts`) because it is installed only on an analysis chat and reads only what that analysis was started on — its one source thread, or the team it was started on: the runs the daemon sampled, and any other run of that team the agent names (user decision: everything of the team can be read, paying only for what is read; a card per page would make the analysis unusable, and the user already pressed Analyze on that team or opened its builder). The slug is the daemon's and `ThreadReaderService.readSourceOf` holds each named run to it, so another team's run, a deleted run and a chat of no team stay refused, and a thread analysis keeps its one thread. Each is read up to its snapshot, beside the team's own ledger figures over its other runs (`view=history`, `view=spend`: no transcript text, no folder path); it still carries no `readOnlyHint`, leads with the history preface and masks secrets.
- `MemoryMcpTool` is the base for the shared memory's tools (`memory_search`, `memory_read`, `memory_save`, `memory_forget`): offered on every endpoint while the user has memory on, refused `MEMORY_DISABLED` at call time once it is off, and given the run's project and the caller's identity by `MemoryService` (never by the arguments). They are auto-approved in chats and team nodes alike (`isHostMemoryCall`); the write limits live in `MemoryService`, not in the approval.
- `KnowledgeMcpTool` is the base for the knowledge store's tools (`knowledge_search`, `knowledge_read`, `knowledge_save`), on the same terms: offered while the user has knowledge on, refused `KNOWLEDGE_DISABLED` at call time once it is off, the run's place and the caller's identity from `KnowledgeService`, unless an analysis, builder or project chat names another place with `project` or `team` (the base takes them out of the arguments before the tool's own reader). A tool fills `ownInstructions` and `ownSchema`, and the base adds those two where they are offered. `knowledge_save` is unlisted while agents may only read. They are auto-approved (`isHostKnowledgeCall`); the write rules live in `KnowledgeService`.
- `BrowserTool` (`tools/browser-shared/browser-tool.ts`) is the base for the in-app browser's seventeen `browser_*` tools: offered while `BrowserBroker.canDrive`, each call run through the broker under `whileCancellable`, its outcome worded once (`readsPage` adds the untrusted-page-content preface). `tools/browser-shared/` holds that base and the family's shared readers and wording, and is the one directory under `tools/` that is not a tool.
- A tool that waits on a person runs the wait through `context.whileCancellable(…)`.
- The only tool not on `BaseMcpTool` is `tools/board/board.tools.ts` (the tasks module owns those tools and this module may not import it). Do not add a second exception.

## Adding a tool

1. Name it as `HOST_<NAME>_TOOL` in `agents/chat.types.ts` if anything outside `v1/mcp` (the permission gate, the renderer) must recognise it.
2. Write the four files; the class extends `BaseMcpTool` or `CallMcpTool`.
3. Register it in `createMcpTools` (`tools/mcp-tools.ts`) — the one place the `tools/list` order is set, and the order is part of what a model reads. New dependencies go in `McpToolDeps` and the `MCP_TOOLS` factory in `mcp.module.ts`.
4. Auto-approval (only when calling it is not itself a decision): an `isHost<Name>Call` predicate in `agents/utils/host-<name>.ts` over `isHostToolCall`, used by `ChatService`'s `autoApproves`. Predicates and any reader `v1/agents` needs stay in `agents/utils`, because `v1/agents` may not import `v1/mcp`.
5. Renderer: a tool whose call row the transcript hides goes in `GENIRO_TOOLS` (`apps/ui/src/renderer/chats/geniro-tool.ts`) — an unchecked map, easy to miss. A call tool also goes in `GENIRO_MCP_CALL_TOOLS` (`agents/adapters/adapter.types.ts`).
6. Description audit (`mcp-server.service.spec.ts`): a tool overlapping another names it in its instructions and is named back; every tool says when to use it; every card tool says when not to.
7. The system instructions: name the tool in `GENIRO_UI_PREAMBLE`'s "Geniro's own tools" section (`agents/utils/agent-instructions.ts`) by the situation it is for, in the same change — claude lists MCP tools by name only, so the preamble is where an agent learns when a tool is the move. Add its `HOST_*` constant to the wire-name list in `agent-instructions.spec.ts`. Only a tool something else already explains (a companion named in another tool's description, or one offered only where a brief names it) is exempted instead, in `PREAMBLE_EXEMPT` (`mcp-server.service.spec.ts`) with that reason; that spec fails on a listed tool that is neither.

## Changing a tool

- Instructions and schema are what every model reads: change wording deliberately and re-run the description audit.
- A tool whose purpose changes, or that is renamed or removed, changes its preamble line in the same change.
- A refactor meant to change nothing must leave `tools/list` and call results byte-identical — prove it by capturing them before and after.
- Reader tests live in `<tool>.reader.spec.ts`; cross-tool behaviour (listing, dispatch, cancellation) in `mcp-server.service.spec.ts`.
